encoding.frame: Requests and responses are [type: uint8][payload length: uint32][payload]. A request's type is its command id, a response's its response id. Each request gets exactly one response, in order.

fieldTypes.bool: 1 byte: 0 is false, 1 is true (readers take any non-zero byte as true).
fieldTypes.string: A uint32 byte count, then that many bytes of UTF-8, with no terminator.
fieldTypes.json: Identical to string on the wire: a uint32 byte count, then UTF-8 JSON text. Written json (any JSON value) or json:<shape>, where a shape is string, number, bool, json (any value), a jsonTypes entry, or a shape followed by []. A jsonTypes entry maps each key to a shape; a key ending in ? is optional. Clients with codecs parse the text; to anything else it is a string.
fieldTypes.bytes: The rest of the payload, with no length prefix. Only ever the last field.
fieldTypes.mat4: 16 float32, column-major (element col * 4 + row) for column vectors, so the translation is elements 12, 13 and 14.
fieldTypes.<type>: An entry of types: its fields in order, with no prefix.
fieldTypes.<type>[]: Elements of <type> back to back, with no length prefix: their number is the uint32 field named count declared before the array.

encoding.errorPayload: An Error response's payload is the message as raw UTF-8 bytes, not a string: the frame's length is the message's byte count.
encoding.reservedIds: Ids 0xC0 to 0xFE are reserved for server-pushed event frames: no command or response uses them.
encoding.versioning: version is major.minor.patch. The minor version goes up for new commands, new responses, new trailing request fields and new trailing response fields; anything else (a changed id, field order or type, a removed field) bumps the major version. Both directions must keep working within a major version: a server reads a trailing request field only when the payload has bytes left and otherwise uses a default, since a client of an older minor version doesn't send it (Commands.hpp: ReadTrailing); a client's decoders ignore response bytes after the fields they know, and a client relies on a response field added in a later minor version only once Hello has shown the server speaks that version. Hello refuses a client whose major version differs from the server's, and accepts any minor version with a warning when it differs.

RenderFrame.description: Renders one frame at the viewport size (SetViewportSize; 1280x720 until it is called). pixels is width * height * 4 bytes of RGBA8, top row first, alpha 255, on every renderer backend, so it can be drawn as-is (e.g. as canvas ImageData).

SetViewportSize.description: Sets the size, in pixels, that later RenderFrame frames are rendered at (each 1 to 4096; anything else is an Error). The renderer itself is resized, so frames are neither cropped nor resampled, and the camera's aspect follows.

Hello.description: Opens a session: the client's name, the protocol version it speaks (its PROTOCOL_VERSION) and the host's access token (empty when it has none). Error when the major versions differ, or when the host requires a token and this isn't it. Optional on a host without a token. On a host with one, every other command (Shutdown included) is refused with an Error until a Hello on the same connection succeeds, and a failed Hello ends the session. The session belongs to the connection: a client that reconnects sends Hello again. capabilities names optional features beyond what the version implies (none are defined yet); projectLoaded is whether the host has a project (was started with --project).

PollEvents.description: Returns the server's events after afterSeq, oldest first: log lines (every line the host logs, from startup on) and, in later versions, other kinds. Each event has a seq, from 1, never reused while the host runs: pass 0 for everything the server still has, then each response's nextSeq. Returns at most maxEvents (and at most 1024) events; nextSeq is the last one's seq, or, when none is returned, the newest seq, so maxEvents 0 skips everything retained. The server keeps the newest 4096 events (and about 2 MiB of them); dropped counts the events after afterSeq that fell off before this poll. An afterSeq newer than any seq the server has issued (from an earlier host process) reads as 0. A client polls it (about every 100 ms); it never logs, so an idle server returns no events. A log event is {seq, kind: "log", level: "info" | "warn" | "error", message, time: Unix milliseconds}; a client ignores kinds and keys it doesn't know.
